facts.value: Daily overtime at 1.5x required after 8 hours worked in any 24-hour period for employees earning less than 1.5x the state minimum wage (below $18.00/hr as of July 2026); employees at or above that rate receive only weekly overtime after 40 hours.
facts.summary: Nevada adds daily overtime after 8 hours in a 24-hour period for lower-wage employees, unlike federal law which only requires overtime after 40 hours per week.
facts.notes: The $18.00/hr daily-OT threshold is 1.5x the $12.00 minimum wage; verify if the minimum wage changes. A written mutual agreement for four 10-hour days can waive daily OT. Numerous occupational exemptions apply.

facts.summary: Nevada's minimum wage is $12.00 per hour, effective July 1, 2026, applying to all employees regardless of employer-offered health benefits.
facts.sourceAgency: Nevada Office of the Labor Commissioner
facts.notes: Ballot Question 2 (2022) eliminated the former two-tier (health-benefit) wage system as of July 1, 2024. Figure confirmed on the official 2026 Annual Minimum Wage Bulletin posted June 29, 2026.

value: hairstyles/traits historically associated with race (CROWN Act)
facts.summary: Beyond the federal protected classes, Nevada also prohibits employment discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, discussing wages, and race-associated hairstyles.
facts.notes: Federal base classes (race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability) are also covered under NRS 613.330. Statute additionally addresses service animals and consideration of criminal history.

facts.summary: Nevada's employment discrimination law applies to employers with 15 or more employees, the same threshold as federal Title VII.
facts.notes: Defined as 15+ employees for each working day in 20+ calendar weeks in the current or preceding year; matches federal coverage.

facts.value: Nevada Pregnant Workers' Fairness Act requires reasonable accommodation for conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition, unless the employer proves undue hardship.
facts.summary: Nevada separately mandates reasonable accommodation of pregnancy and childbirth-related conditions and bars adverse action for requesting such accommodation.
facts.notes: Applies to employers with 15+ employees. NRS 613.4374 sets the undue-hardship standard; NRS 613.438 prohibits adverse action for accommodation requests. Disability accommodation otherwise tracks federal ADA under NRS 613.330.

facts.value: Unlawful for an employer to discriminate against an employee or applicant because they opposed an unlawful employment practice or participated in a related investigation, proceeding, or hearing.
facts.summary: Nevada statute independently prohibits retaliation against workers who oppose discrimination or take part in discrimination proceedings.
facts.notes: Parallels federal Title VII anti-retaliation protection but exists as an independent state cause of action.

facts.summary: An employee may bring a civil action for unpaid wages within 2 years of the employer's failure to pay.
facts.notes: Statute of limitations for private civil wage actions under Chapter 608.

facts.summary: An employment discrimination charge must be filed with the Nevada Equal Rights Commission within 300 days of the alleged discriminatory act.
facts.notes: 300-day figure confirmed via official DETR/NERC guidance; the direct PDF returned 403 but the deadline is stated on the official DETR File a Charge page. NRS 613.430 also sets limits on subsequent civil actions.

facts.value: Discharged employees must be paid all earned, unpaid wages immediately; employees who quit must be paid by the earlier of the next regular payday or 7 days after quitting. A waiting-time penalty of continued wages (up to 30 days) applies for late payment.
facts.summary: Nevada sets strict deadlines for final pay -- immediately on discharge and within 7 days (or next payday) on resignation -- with a penalty for late payment, unlike federal law which sets no final-pay timing.
facts.notes: NRS 608.040 waiting-time penalty accrues at the employee's rate for up to 30 days when the employer fails to pay on time.
